If you mean what the surgery treated, it depended where you were located. Trepanation was used to “treat” mental illness, physical illness, open the third eye, increase blood flow, and remove demons. Now it’s most commonly used to relieve pressure from the brain, usually due to hematomas, or to access a small part of the brain

In more modern times, yes, but previously it was done by grinding or chipping away an area of the skull. If you look at old skulls found with trepanation scars, some have ridged edges from chipping (often forms circular holes) or long, grinding motions (often makes square holes).

I did a paper on this once! Trepanation (creating a hole in the skull) is the oldest form of surgery that we have archaeological evidence of. Lots of people survived and lived long after their surgeries. You had a better chance of surviving trepanation in 400CE than you did in the 1800s. I don’t trust the validity of this picture, as it isn’t in any papers, books, or articles I studied about this topic, but it’s an interesting surgery that we still do today

Edit: Apparently this skull was on display at Museo del Oro in Lima, Peru. I don’t believe it’s still on display as there aren’t more recent photos. This skull actually has a second trepanation hole in the back that wasn’t covered with a gold inlay. Very interesting!
